calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Blues are the league’s best for chance quality, and the Avalanche are one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Blues still get theirs.
calls.call: The Blues’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Avalanche.
calls.nums: St. Louis 1st for chance quality (a 7.0% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Colorado 3rd for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On chance quality, St. Louis had 5.1% a shot. The league average is 6.3% a shot, and they came in at 7.0% a shot.

calls.head: The Avalanche will outshoot the Blues
calls.body: The Avalanche are the league’s best for shot volume, at the relentless end; the Blues are near the bottom of the league, at the selective end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Avalanche take more 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than the Blues.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, Colorado had 74.6 per 60 and St. Louis 56.4 per 60. Coming in, Colorado was at 68.4 per 60 and St. Louis at 53.7 per 60.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 72% chance, and Colorado delivered.

STL.head: We gave St. Louis only a 28% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: St. Louis couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: St. Louis’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 5.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 7.0% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

surprises.head: St. Louis tried a different line
surprises.body: D. Dube, P. Suter, Z. Dean played 10:26 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of St. Louis’s usual lines.

story.head: The Avalanche roll past the Blues
paras: Cale Makar opened the scoring early in the first. Martin Necas added two goals. Five different Avalanche scored.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Avalanche win about four in five. The Blues tried a line they hadn’t used before: Dillon Dube, Pius Suter and Zach Dean.

items.text: Whether the Blues keep that line together in Chicago on Tuesday.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
